references.text: Also describes the promised land as a land of streams, springs, and water flowing out in the valleys and on the mountains.
The preceding verse contrasts Egypt with the promised land and explains that the new land is different from Egypt.
Mentions the plain of Sharon and the valley of Achor as grazing lands, highlighting the country's varied topography with plains and valleys.
Describes how rain and snow come down from heaven to water the earth, paralleling the description of the land drinking water from the rain of heaven.
Encourages praying to the Lord for rain in the spring rainy season and shows God's control over the rain from heaven.
Describes how God waters the mountains from his high chambers and the earth is satisfied with the fruit of his works.
The continuation promises that God will give rain to the land at the right time, both the autumn rain and the spring rain.
God's promise to send rain at the right time as a blessing over the land.
